core_obligations: Start from the prepared diagram (proof lines 17325-17327): the author takes a diagram and an abelian sheaf annihilated by n as produced by the companion preparation lemma, so that the base change map fails in degree q.
Normalizations of the base (proof lines 17328-17329): the base S' may be assumed affine, which the author notes is immediate.
Algebraically closed residue field (proof lines 17330-17331): by the integral top lemma the field K may be assumed algebraically closed.

Constant coefficients (proof lines 17332-17335): the sheaf then corresponds to a module over the cyclic group of order n, which decomposes as a direct sum of copies of the cyclic modules of order dividing n, so the sheaf may be assumed constant with value a cyclic group of order d dividing n.
Normal base (proof lines 17336-17338): by the integral bottom lemma the base S' may be replaced by its normalization in the spectrum of K, which completes the construction.
proof_roadmap: Use the companion preparation lemma to obtain a diagram and a sheaf where base change already fails.
Reduce to an affine base and then, through the integral top lemma, to an algebraically closed field.
Reduce the coefficients to a constant cyclic sheaf and, through the integral bottom lemma, to a normal affine base.
difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the failure of the base change property concrete: if the property holds in degree q - 1 but fails in degree q, then there is a cartesian diagram with an affine, integral, normal base with algebraically closed function field, a dominant map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, and a cyclic coefficient sheaf of order dividing n whose higher direct image in degree q does not vanish (statement lines 17295-17317). The proof is a complete chain of named reductions: it starts from the diagram and sheaf prepared by the companion lemma (proof lines 17325-17327), makes the base affine (proof lines 17328-17329), makes the field algebraically closed through the integral top lemma (proof lines 17330-17331), replaces the coefficients by a constant cyclic sheaf using the decomposition of modules over the cyclic group (proof lines 17332-17335), and replaces the base by its normalization in that field through the integral bottom lemma (proof lines 17336-17338). The non-formal content is the sequence of reductions, each attributed. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with every input named.
